yours:
Ryan texted me at midnight. He said we needed to talk. I knew right away what that meant.

The next day we met at a coffee shop downtown. He was already there, scrolling on his phone. He looked nervous. He said he wasn't ready for something serious. He said it wasn't me, it was him.

I wanted to cry but I didn't. I just nodded and said okay. Then I walked home in the rain and ate a whole pint of ice cream.

My roommate thought I was overreacting. Maybe I was. But it still hurt.
rewrite:
Ryan sent me word at midnight that we must talk; and I understood at once, without taking to be told, what such a message must mean.

We met the next day at a coffee-house in the town, where I found him already arrived, and occupied with the little instrument in his hand. He looked nervous; and he said that he was not ready for anything serious, and that the fault was not in me, but in himself.

I wanted to cry, but did not; I only nodded, and said that it was all very well; and then I walked home in the rain, and ate a whole pint of ice cream, which was, I believe, the most rational thing I did that day.

The friend with whom I lodged thought I made a great deal too much of it, and perhaps I did; but it was not the less painful for that.

Hi team,

Quick update: the launch is moving from Tuesday to Thursday. Legal still hasn't signed off on the pricing page, and I don't want us shipping without it.

Please have your sections of the deck done by Wednesday at noon. If you're blocked, tell me today, not tomorrow.

Sam

My dear friends,

I must give you notice that our undertaking is put off from Tuesday to Thursday; for the lawyers have not yet given their approval to the paper of terms, and I would by no means have us send anything abroad without it.

I must beg you, therefore, to have your several parts of the papers finished by Wednesday at noon; and if anything should hinder you, pray let me know of it today, and not tomorrow, when the knowledge of it could be of no very great use.

With many thanks, Sam

faults.quote: the lawyers have not yet given their approval to the paper of terms

faults.quote: send anything abroad without it

faults.why: This is a usable exercise, but it does not warn that understatement can weaken clarity in a work email with a real deadline. It also does not teach how to preserve concrete nouns such as “pricing page” and “deck” while borrowing Austen’s sentence shape.

Hi team,

rewrite:
Unto you my fellowlabourers, greeting.

Behold, I make known unto you in few words, that the launch shall not be on Tuesday, but on Thursday. For the lawyers have not yet given their word upon the pricing page; and I will not that we send forth the work without it.

Wherefore let every one of you finish his part of the deck by Wednesday at noon: and if ye be hindered in any thing, tell me this day, and tarry not until the morrow.

I give you thanks. The salutation of me Sam with mine own hand.

notes.text: The Bible has no word 'team', so I named the readers by the work they share, the way Paul greets his helpers in Philemon.

rows.text: Behold, I make known unto you in few words, that the launch shall not be on Tuesday, but on Thursday. For the lawyers have not yet given their word upon the pricing page; and I will not that we send forth the work without it.

rows.text: I give you thanks. The salutation of me Sam with mine own hand.

notes.text: This is the way an epistle signs off (2 Thessalonians 3:17). It stands for the bare name at the foot of the email.
notes.after: The salutation of me Sam with mine own hand.

lessons: Your email is a string of short, separate orders. The Bible's manner puts each order where it follows from the one before. "Behold" calls the team to look at the news, "For the lawyers have not yet given their word" gives the reason in the same breath, and "Wherefore let every one of you" makes the deadlines the natural result of the delay, not a fresh demand. To practise this, write your news, give your reason with "for", and then begin your request with "so" or "wherefore", so the reader feels each step lead to the next.

plan.why: An epistle opens by naming who it is for and greeting them, all in one line.

plan.gist: behold, the day is moved; for the lawyers have not yet given their word
plan.why: The news comes first, called out with 'behold', and the reason follows straight after with 'for', as the Bible's letters do it.

plan.gist: wherefore finish the deck; and if hindered, tell me this day
plan.why: 'Wherefore' makes the requests follow from the news, and 'and' joins the two requests into one sentence.

plan.gist: thanks, and the salutation in his own hand
plan.why: An epistle ends with thanks and the writer's own name.

faults.quote: Behold, I make known unto you in few words
faults.why: This is a generalized biblical pastiche rather than a strongly KJV-shaped epistolary opening. KJV epistles more characteristically use formulas such as “I would not have you ignorant,” “I certify you,” or “I would have you know,” rather than this assembled phrasing.

faults.quote: I give you thanks.
faults.why: This is not idiomatic KJV wording for a closing. The KJV commonly has “I thank my God,” “we give thanks,” or a benediction; “I give you thanks” sounds like a literal modern-English substitution and is faintly awkward.

faults.quote: the lawyers have not yet given their word upon the pricing page
faults.why: “Legal” is rendered as “the lawyers,” which is plausible, but “given their word” is less exact than having “signed off”: it can mean merely offering an opinion or promise rather than formally approving the page.

faults.quote: I will not that we send forth the work without it
faults.why: “It” has a potentially unstable antecedent: grammatically it may refer to “the pricing page” rather than Legal’s approval. The source specifically says Sam does not want shipping without Legal’s sign-off.

faults.quote: “Behold, I make known unto you in few words, that the launch shall not be on Tuesday, but on Thursday.” — cites Galatians 1:20
faults.why: The citation is inapt. Galatians 1:20 reads, “Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not”; it does not support “make known unto you” or “in few words.”

faults.quote: Behold, lo, verily
faults.why: The note lists “lo” and “verily,” but neither occurs in the quoted rewrite. It therefore does not accurately name the actual move.

faults.quote: “Wherefore let every one of you finish his part of the deck by Wednesday at noon” — cites 1 Samuel 30:24
faults.why: 1 Samuel 30:24 contains “as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff,” not a comparable “Wherefore let every one...” exhortation. The citation does not substantiate the claimed syntax.

faults.quote: “and if ye be hindered in any thing, tell me this day, and tarry not until the morrow.” — cites Judges 6:18
faults.why: Judges 6:18 says “Depart not hence, I pray thee, until I come unto thee,” and is not a good source for the stated paratactic pattern or the wording “tarry ... until the morrow.”

faults.quote: “if ye be hindered” — cites Luke 11:52
faults.why: Luke 11:52 does not illustrate this second-person passive form; it concerns lawyers taking away “the key of knowledge.” The source attribution is inaccurate.

faults.quote: Your email is a string of short, separate orders.
faults.why: This misdescribes the original. Its launch news and reason are already joined in one sentence, and its two requests are organized as a deadline followed by a contingency. The lesson should identify a real stylistic opportunity rather than characterize the draft unfairly.

faults.quote: “Wherefore let every one of you” makes the deadlines the natural result of the delay
faults.why: The lesson overstates the logical relation. The delayed launch may make the Wednesday deadline sensible, but the source does not explicitly present the deck deadline as a consequence of the legal delay. This teaches connective rhetoric at the cost of slightly inventing the argument.

judge.verdict: The rewrite preserves the email’s essential facts, sequence, requests, and form, and its broad biblical-epistolary manner is serviceable. Its weakest aspect is the instructional apparatus: several claimed sources are wrong or poorly matched, and the lesson inaccurately diagnoses the original’s structure.
